newsitem.title: UK: Tesco plays down planned Autumn price move.
newsitem.headline: Tesco plays down planned Autumn price move.

text.p: Supermarket group Tesco Plc on Tuesday played down market rumours that the group is poised to launch a new price campaign, saying its plans did not go beyond Autumn initiatives common for UK food retailers.
Its shares rallied from yesterday's decline, driven in part by market talk of a new price-cutting campanign, to be up 1p at 301by 0953 GMT.

"In the autumn all retailers have promotions and like other companies we have plans," a spokesman told Reuters. But the spokesman declined to give any further details and said the planned moves were not out of the ordinary.
"We always offer excellent value for money and we will continue to do so," he said.

The continuing intense competition among UK supermarket companies was highlighted last month as J.Sainsbury Plc said it was seeing a sales lift of approximately two or three percent following the launch of its Reward loyalty card in June.
Deputy chief executive Dino Adiano told Reuters there was "no doubt the introduction of the Reward card... has been hugely successful."
Tesco's earlier introduction of its ClubCard loyalty card was credited with helping it pull ahead of arch-rival Sainsbury in terms of market share earlier this year.
A spokeswoman for Sainsbury said the company on Sunday began its "Autumn Value" promotion offering discounts and special offers on a range of everyday products.
Such autumn campaigns are seen as a way for supermarket groups to grab consumers' attention in the run-up to the heavy-spending Christmas period.
